dataset_or_source: UHOP Schedule E-1 and RHOP Schedule D land-use designations
finding: No public machine-readable layer exists for Hamilton's citywide Official Plan land-use designations (UHOP Schedule E-1 urban and RHOP Schedule D rural). The City's plan pages offer PDFs only.
evidence: Live ?f=json and /query checks 2026-10-17 | all 1,697 layers on spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services | all 594 services in Hamilton's ArcGIS Online org (covers open.hamilton.ca) | McMaster | Mohawk | UWaterloo | Hamilton Conservation Authority | Ontario GeoHub: none carry E-1 or D designations | Schedule E is Urban Structure and the designations are on E-1
implication: Citywide designation is a named gap. Fill by requesting the internal layer from the City (authoritative) or by vector extraction from the schedule PDFs (see PI-0007). Use secondary plan land use (PI-0002) and Employment Lands (PI-0004) meanwhile.

dataset_or_source: Hamilton PolicyPlanning MapServer layer 6 (Secondary Plan Land Use)
finding: Public secondary plan land-use layer covers all 31 secondary plans with 67 land-use classes.
evidence: https://spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services/General/PolicyPlanning/MapServer/6 | 47,212 polygons | 31 plans | 67 classes | latest amendment date 2026-05-12 (live read 2026-10-17)
implication: Usable now for designation context inside secondary plan areas. Needs the cleanup in PI-0003 before display.

dataset_or_source: Hamilton PolicyPlanning MapServer layer 6 (Secondary Plan Land Use)
finding: Layer is cut to individual lots (median about 814 m2) so polygons need dissolving by plan and class. Four retired plans are still present and must be filtered. Plan names do not exactly match the companion secondary plan boundary layer. Downtown Hamilton may be out of date. Not listed on open.hamilton.ca and no licence stated.
evidence: https://spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services/General/PolicyPlanning/MapServer/6 | median polygon area about 814 m2 | 4 retired plans present | name mismatch vs boundary layer (live read 2026-10-17)
implication: Dissolve and filter retired plans in normalize. Build a plan-name crosswalk to the boundary layer. Record licence as not stated (licences are not a gate, Morgen 2026-10-17).

finding: Employment Lands layer has 22 polygons grouped by named employment district. The City says they are based on the Schedule E-1 employment designations, but they are not drawn per designation.
evidence: Employment_Lands/FeatureServer/2 in Hamilton's ArcGIS Online org | 22 polygons (live read 2026-10-17)
implication: Partial proxy for E-1 employment designations at district grain only. Pair with the 2019 Provincially Significant Employment Zones layer.

finding: The City's own planning viewers pull from an internal server that has no public DNS and cannot be reached from outside. Its policy-planning service has more layers than the public copy, but no layer title visible in those maps is an E-1 or D designation.
evidence: Viewer app configs reference itvpgisappint.hamilton.ca | no public DNS resolution (checked 2026-10-17)
implication: Do not retry from outside (HARD-RULES 9). The only route is a request to the City for the internal designation layer.

finding: A search hit that looked like a Hamilton 2019 Official Plan Schedule E layer belongs to Thunder Bay, not Hamilton.
implication: Exclude from Hamilton candidates. Confirm the owning municipality of ArcGIS search hits before cataloguing.

dataset_or_source: UHOP Schedule E-1 and RHOP Schedule D PDFs
finding: The schedule PDFs are vector CorelDRAW exports, not scans, so the coloured designation polygons can be extracted directly from the file and georeferenced using road intersections.
evidence: Schedule E-1 and D PDFs from hamilton.ca inspected 2026-10-17 | vector paths present | no embedded georeferencing | legend categories extracted for comparison with GIS layers
implication: Viable fallback for the PI-0001 gap. See effort estimate PI-0008.

dataset_or_source: UHOP Schedule E-1 and RHOP Schedule D PDFs
finding: Vector extraction plus georeferencing of both schedules is estimated at about 6-7 person-days, versus about 12-15 person-days of hand tracing.
evidence: Estimate from inspection of the vector PDFs 2026-10-17
implication: Prefer vector extraction over tracing. Also request the internal layer from the City, since it is the only authoritative source.

dataset_or_source: UHOP Schedule E-1 and RHOP Schedule D PDFs
finding: The schedule PDFs carry a Teranet copyright notice. The public secondary plan layer (PI-0002) has no stated licence.
evidence: Copyright notice on the schedule PDFs (checked 2026-10-17)
implication: Recorded for provenance only. Licences are not a gate per Morgen's 2026-10-17 rule (HARD-RULES 6).

dataset_or_source: NPCA assessment parcels vs City of Hamilton parcels
finding: NPCA and Hamilton city parcels show a constant offset of about 0.98 m (Hamilton about 0.30 m east and 0.94 m south of NPCA), likely a datum difference. Shifting by that vector gives 100% overlap.
evidence: Grok Bot comparison of NPCA and City of Hamilton parcel layers clipped to Hamilton (local-data only)
implication: Apply or account for the shift before spatial joins between NPCA-derived and City parcels. Centre-point joins tolerate it for now.
